title: Osteoporosis: integrated risk, treatment and follow-up algorithm
purpose: Clinician-reviewed decision support; not a validated autonomous prescribing engine.
scope: Postmenopausal women and men aged 50 years or older.

provenance.baseline: Risk thresholds and treatment framework transcribed from the three supplied SEIOMM-based figures.
provenance.supplement: Special-scenario interpretation informed by NOGG and KDIGO. This is a synthesis, not a single society's validated algorithm.

items: Fragility fracture site, number and dates
DXA at hip and lumbar spine
Glucocorticoid dose in prednisolone equivalents and duration
Current osteoporosis therapy, duration, adherence and response
assessment.missing_data: Do not interpret unknown values as negative. If missing information could change classification, return assessment_incomplete.

any_of: Hip or vertebral fracture with T-score < -3.0

high.condition: No baseline very-high-risk criterion and at least one high-risk criterion
any_of: Other fragility fracture, including humeral or pelvic fracture
Hip or vertebral fracture not meeting very-high-risk criteria
FRAX above applicable national treatment threshold

below_threshold_or_incomplete.condition: No identified criterion; distinguish fully assessed below-threshold patients from incomplete assessments

baseline_classification.threshold_note: Strict < -3.5 retained from supplied table. NOGG separately uses <= -3.5 as a very-high-risk indicator. Do not silently substitute thresholds across guidelines.

mandatory_special_scenario_review.timing: Before final risk classification and before treatment selection; repeat during follow-up
principles: No universal one-category upgrade for all modifiers.
No additive point score or invented FRAX multiplier.
Existing very-high-risk status is not downgraded by absence of special scenarios.
Pending clinical review must not default to low risk or automatic treatment.
An upgrade prompts specialist assessment and consideration of bone-forming therapy, not mandatory anabolic treatment.

branches.action: Flag very-high-risk indicator and specialist assessment under NOGG, even without very low BMD.
Reassess site, age, BMD, falls and other risk factors; possible upgrade after clinical review, not automatic very high risk solely from recency.

scenarios.trigger: Systemic prednisolone-equivalent >=5 mg/day in supplied table
scenarios.effect: Dose- and duration-dependent risk; assess glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis

branches.action: Flag NOGG very-high-risk indicator; prompt specialist assessment.
Review dose, duration, fractures, BMD and applicable glucocorticoid guidance; do not automatically label very high risk.

scenarios.note: The >=5 mg/day source flag is not a universal treatment threshold. Lower doses may still warrant assessment.

scenarios.trigger: Frequent falls or high falls risk
scenarios.effect: May increase risk beyond standard FRAX, which does not directly include falls
scenarios.action: Consider upgrade when combined with high baseline risk, frailty, low BMD or recent fracture; provide falls assessment and prevention.

scenarios.trigger: New fragility fracture during osteoporosis treatment
scenarios.action: Review adherence, adequate treatment exposure, administration, secondary causes and BMD response; consider escalation or specialist referral.
Individualize fracture assessment; evaluate calcium, phosphate, PTH and alkaline phosphatase with renal/bone specialist input as appropriate. Assess bone turnover and drug suitability.
scenarios.note: CKD-MBD can require a dedicated pathway rather than routine osteoporosis prescribing.

routing.condition: Assessment or necessary clinical review incomplete
routing.next: Complete assessment; do not auto-prescribe or assign low risk.
Specialist assessment; consider initial bone-forming therapy, individualized to approvals and suitability.

routing.condition: Final category below_treatment_threshold and review complete

consider.note: Source duration; local approved duration varies.

very_high.sequence: Immediately follow a completed bone-forming course with an appropriate antiresorptive.

high.preferred: Oral or IV bisphosphonate, if suitable
high.alternative: Denosumab with a planned long-term and exit strategy

formal_duration_review.denosumab: 5–10 years or target attainment; continue routine review throughout

persistent_high_risk.additional_requirement: Reassess current clinical risk and all special scenarios before continuation or pause decisions.

if_persistent_high_risk.oral_bisphosphonate: Consider continuation up to 10 years total, individualized
if_persistent_high_risk.iv_bisphosphonate: Consider continuation up to 6 years total, individualized
if_persistent_high_risk.new_fracture: Reassess causes, exposure and need for treatment change.

if_low_or_controlled_risk.bisphosphonate: Consider monitored pause for 1–3 years, individualized to agent and risk
if_low_or_controlled_risk.denosumab: No drug holiday. If stopping, arrange planned transition to a potent bisphosphonate when suitable; specialist plan if contraindicated.

safety_rules: Never stop denosumab without a planned subsequent antiresorptive strategy.
Advanced CKD is not an automatic indication for anabolic therapy.
A single on-treatment fracture does not automatically establish treatment failure.
Risk upgrade does not bypass drug contraindications or local prescribing approvals.
